primary_rec_title: Add explicit prebolus and at-meal bolus to replace SMB-only meal coverage
summary: 14-day Nightscout/AAPS audit (Aug 7–21, 2026). CGM coverage 98.7%, data quality good. Overall glucose control: TIR 86%, moderate variability (CV 32.6%). Overnight and morning fasting control are good; basal schedule is appropriate. No carb entries recorded; UAM detects meals late or incompletely. profile_rec_text: Lower ISF baseline from 56 to 40 mg/dL/U; reduce DIA from 10 to 8 hours. meal_suggestion: Implement prebolus meal management combined with meal logging. Current observed strategy is reactive (no prebolus, SMB/UAM-driven) due to zero meal logging. Rationale: With zero meal logging and no prebolus, system is forced to rely entirely on SMB (every 3 min) to manage meal carbs arriving during or after bolus time. This results in 40–90 mg/dL early peaks and requires aggressive Dynamic ISF compression to correct. Prebolus delivers insulin proactively, suppressing early carb absorption. Meal logging enables correct bolus sizing and prevents SMB from guessing meal intent. Together, these reduce afternoon highs from 148–162 mg/dL to <130 mg/dL (estimated) and reduce SMB workload. Confidence in this recommendation is medium-high (85%) because observed meal patterns (delayed peaks, SMB-driven recovery) are consistent; however, actual implementation success depends on user adherence and meal logging accuracy.

Primary recommendation is to lower baseline ISF from 56 to 40 mg/dL/U, reduce DIA from 10 to 8 hours, and add systematic meal logging and 5–10 min prebolus to enable proactive control. summary: User with type 1 diabetes on AAPS closed-loop therapy with GLP-1 (semaglutide 1.25 mg weekly) shows 86.0% time-in-range over 14 days but persistent midday hyperglycemia (hours 12-17, avg 135-162 mg/dL) and hypoglycemia clusters (hours 1, 18-19, 23; TBR 5.1%). Telemetry reveals three profile-level defects: basal rate at 16:00 is undersized (0.5 U/h vs. estimated need ≥0.7 U/h for midday plateau); insulin sensitivity factor (ISF) 56 mg/dL/U is too low by 2.5-5× relative to observed correction bolus responses (implied ISF 150-300 mg/dL/U); and DIA 10 hours may be excessive for small microboluses (<0.2 U), causing IOB overestimation and SMB suppression. meal_suggestion: Current observed strategy: Zero prebolus; zero immediate bolus; 100% SMB/UAM meal bolus; no e-carbs. Carb-less operation using UAM detection (glucose delta-triggered SMB micro-boluses every 3 min). This is adaptive and working within the constraint of no carb logging. Immediate bolus captures fast carbs quickly (reduces reliance on imprecise UAM detection). SMB/UAM continues to fine-tune and handle residual carbs, second-wave absorption, and corrections. E-carbs for lunch addresses observed rebound pattern (94→188 mg/dL at 120–240 min), consistent with two-phase absorption (fast carbs absorbed 0–90 min, slow carbs arriving at 120+ min). Keep SMB enabled and interval at 3 min; UAM enabled for unlogged meals or unexpected carbs. Keep Dynamic ISF enabled (70%) during transition to carb-logged mode; reduce to 50% post-validation if glucose stabilizes.

Primary recommendation: implement carbohydrate logging to enable carb-logged meal strategy (prebolus, split bolus, e-carbs for multi-phase meals); verify profile afterward.
